gedanken_release_summary.branch_control_effect: Gedanken packets may affect branch control only through validated follow-up queue items, transfer verdicts, and qualitative graph annotations. They are not counted as proof progress unless a later derivation, computation, or source-backed certificate discharges the relevant obligation.

argument_spine: State the reached milestone and its exact certification evidence.
Identify the same-theory gauge-field object carrying construction, reconstruction, nontriviality, and spectral content.
Present the mathematical bridge lemmas used to move from Euclidean Schwinger data and gauge-invariant observables to the milestone claim.
List disqualifier tests and how each was ruled out.
State remaining obligations and the boundary between achieved progress and unresolved Clay target commitments.
paper_argument.claim_scope: A paper argument is activated only for milestones with certification evidence attached to the same continuum Yang-Mills object: the gauge-field construction, OS reconstruction, nontriviality witness, and spectral-gap witness must all be read from one limiting theory. Until then, the draft records the intended argument shape without claiming a proof.

strategy_learning_summary.decision: Keep this as the mathematical endpoint and derivation checkpoint, but do not promote it as the primary proof route.
strategy_learning_summary.headline: First we tried to express the goal as a bounded Hamiltonian spectral-gap subclaim.
strategy_learning_summary.moved_to: Euclidean correlator decay plus OS/transfer machinery, because it offers a possible witness for the Hamiltonian spectral lower bound.
non_payoff: This did not pay off as a proof route because it described the endpoint more than the construction mechanism.
X: the Hamiltonian formulation presupposes the reconstructed continuum Hilbert space rather than constructing it.
Y: the key inequality E_H((0,Delta)) P_perp = 0 is the hard mass-gap lemma itself, so naming it does not discharge it.
Z: a fixed-lattice transfer-matrix gap may disappear as the cutoff is removed, and gauge-invariant observables may fail to determine the full excitation spectrum.
strategy_learning_summary.physics_story: This is the clean energy-spectrum formulation of the Clay target. Once Euclidean Yang-Mills has produced OS-positive Schwinger functions, reconstruction should give the physical Hilbert space of gauge-invariant states, the vacuum vector, time translations, and a positive Hamiltonian. A mass gap means that after removing the vacuum line there are no arbitrarily soft physical excitations: the first glueball-like gauge-invariant energy lies at least Delta above the vacuum.
what_we_learned: We learned that Hamiltonian language is indispensable as an endpoint test but weak as a discovery engine unless the reconstruction inputs are already available.
A claimed gap must always be asked backwards: where did H_YM, Omega, H, P_perp, and the observable algebra come from?
This converted the analysis from naming a desired spectral inequality into tracking the Euclidean construction and reconstruction prerequisites that make the inequality meaningful.

strategy_learning_summary.decision: Keep this route in the active proof queue, but require uniformity and spectral-determining observables before treating it as progress.
strategy_learning_summary.headline: Then we moved to Euclidean correlator decay as a spectral-gap witness.
strategy_learning_summary.moved_to: Balaban/RG continuum control, because correlator decay is not enough unless it survives into the same continuum object.
non_payoff: It did not pay off as a standalone proof route because Euclidean decay can be true in a regulated or strong-coupling regime without proving a continuum Yang-Mills mass gap.
It left two hidden assumptions exposed: the decay constants must not vanish under cutoff removal, and the observable family must determine the whole physical excitation spectrum.
It also did not by itself supply nontriviality; an exponentially decaying sector is not enough if the limiting theory is Gaussian, empty, or not the constructed Yang-Mills object.
strategy_learning_summary.physics_story: This is the Euclidean physics face of a gap. If a gauge-invariant observable O creates physical excitations from the vacuum, its connected Euclidean time correlation is a Laplace transform of the Hamiltonian spectral measure seen by O. Exponential decay with a cutoff-independent rate says that this spectral measure has no weight near zero. The route is physically meaningful only if the observables survive the continuum limit and are rich enough to see the vacuum-orthogonal excitation sector.
what_we_learned: Correlator decay is valuable only when it is a same-theory spectral witness: the observables, OS reconstruction, and Hamiltonian must all come from the same limiting Schwinger functions.
The right mathematical object to demand next is not just a decay estimate, but a cutoff-uniform decay-to-spectrum lemma with an observable-density hypothesis.
This taught the loop to treat strong-coupling lattice decay as evidence-task material until it carries a continuum-transfer certificate.

strategy_learning_summary.decision: Keep this route in the active proof queue as the construction spine.
strategy_learning_summary.headline: In parallel we moved to Balaban RG as the continuum-construction spine.
strategy_learning_summary.moved_to: Fuse RG continuum control with correlator-decay/spectral transfer rather than treating them as separate successes.
non_payoff: It did not pay off as a mass-gap route by itself because ultraviolet/RG stability is not the same thing as an infrared spectral threshold.
It still leaves the OS/Wightman bridge open: a controlled effective action sequence must produce Schwinger functions with the axioms needed for reconstruction.
It can falsely look like progress if the loop celebrates multiscale control while never extracting a gauge-invariant decay or spectral witness.
strategy_learning_summary.physics_story: This is the scale-dynamics side. Starting with regulated gauge fields, the RG analysis must show that integrating out short-distance modes does not lose control of the non-Abelian interaction, does not break the gauge-invariant observable algebra, and has a continuum limit as the lattice spacing goes to zero and the volume goes to infinity. For the Clay problem, ultraviolet stability is not yet the explanation of the gap; it is the condition under which there is a nontrivial continuum vacuum whose correlations could carry a gap.
what_we_learned: Balaban-style control should be used as the construction spine, not as a substitute for the mass-gap mechanism.
The decisive test is whether RG-controlled cutoff objects produce OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions and a non-Gaussian same-theory witness.
This shifted the loop toward an RG-to-OS bridge lemma instead of adding more renormalisation vocabulary.

strategy_learning_summary.decision: The next iteration should produce explicit bridge-lemma packets, not another broad slogan.
strategy_learning_summary.headline: Now the recursive strategy is to fuse construction and spectral transfer.
strategy_learning_summary.moved_to: OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions plus gauge-invariant spectral-determining observables.
non_payoff: It keeps the continuum object, OS reconstruction, nontriviality witness, and Hamiltonian gap in the same theory.
It prevents drift into pure Hamiltonian notation without construction.
It prevents drift into lattice-only decay without continuum spectral meaning.
strategy_learning_summary.physics_story: The bridge has to say how a continuum gauge theory constructed by scale control becomes a spectral statement. The same limiting Schwinger functions must satisfy reflection positivity, define the gauge-invariant observable algebra, retain a non-Gaussian connected sector, and have Euclidean time correlations whose spectral measures avoid a neighborhood of zero. Only then can the reconstructed Hamiltonian inherit a positive lower threshold.
what_we_learned: The analysis should now advance by testing typed bridge lemmas, not by accumulating more route families.

A strategy only counts as learning if it changes the mathematical dependency order: Hamiltonian claims move behind reconstruction gates, decay claims move behind uniformity/density gates, and RG claims move behind OS/nontriviality gates.
The next useful artifact is therefore a bridge-lemma packet with definitions, assumptions, equations, failure tests, and conditional skill triggers.

strategy_learning_summary.decision: Keep all three reductio branches active as proof-obligation pressure tests, not as proof results.
strategy_learning_summary.headline: We then added reductio branches to test whether the negated worlds create real mathematical pressure.
non_payoff: No contradiction branch currently proves Yang-Mills; each branch is only promotable as a proof obligation.
The no-gap reductio still depends on observable density and cutoff-uniform decay.
The OS and triviality reductios still depend on closedness of reflection positivity and a same-theory nontriviality witness.
strategy_learning_summary.physics_story: A reductio is physically useful only when the negated world leaves a detectable trace. If there is no gap, there should be a sequence of vacuum-orthogonal gauge-invariant states with energies tending to zero, or equivalently spectral weight accumulating at the origin for some determining observable family. If OS positivity fails, the Euclidean theory cannot reconstruct a positive-norm quantum Hilbert space. If the continuum limit is trivial, connected gauge-invariant cumulants collapse. These are physical failure modes, not just logical negations.
what_we_learned: The loop learned to use contradiction as a disciplined pressure test rather than an excuse to skip construction.
A branch succeeds only if the contradiction target is accepted or validator-backed in the same theory.
A failed branch is still valuable when it tells us whether to pivot toward density, closedness, nontriviality, or uniform-decay evidence.

trigger_policy.proof_safety_rule: The paper draft must distinguish certified progress from a full Yang-Mills proof unless all Clay commitments are discharged in the same theory.
trigger_policy.required_action: When any success milestone enters a reached status, retain a LaTeX process summary and a paper-argument draft.

certification_evidence: Uniform multiscale/RG bounds across the cutoff-removal sequence.
Tightness or convergence argument for the regulated measures or Schwinger functions.
Reflection positivity survives the limiting procedure.
disqualifiers: Only finite-volume or fixed-lattice-spacing control is available.
The limit is not shown to be a quantum Yang-Mills object on R^4.
Gauge-group structure is lost or replaced by a scalar/free surrogate.
watched_milestones.label: Continuum Yang-Mills object constructed
watched_milestones.next_action: Formulate the exact continuum-passage lemma connecting Balaban-style estimates to OS-positive limiting Schwinger functions.
watched_milestones.potentially_achieved_when: A Balaban/RG-controlled cutoff sequence is shown to have a continuum limit with OS-positive Schwinger functions for compact simple gauge group Yang-Mills on R^4.
watched_milestones.success_signal: Cutoff-removal theorem with a named limiting object S_n and preserved gauge-invariant observables.
watched_milestones.why_big_deal: This would attack the existence half of the Clay target rather than only optimizing a regulated lattice model.

certification_evidence: Reflection positivity for the limiting Schwinger functions.
Euclidean covariance, symmetry, regularity, and clustering assumptions required by the reconstruction theorem.
Explicit identification of gauge-invariant observable classes carried into the Hilbert space.
disqualifiers: The Hilbert space is postulated rather than reconstructed.
The reconstruction applies to a different regulated theory.
The observable class is too small to speak about the physical excitation spectrum.
watched_milestones.label: OS reconstruction yields the physical Hilbert space
watched_milestones.next_action: Write the OS reconstruction obligation as a bridge lemma with inputs, theorem used, and output objects H_YM, Omega, H.
watched_milestones.potentially_achieved_when: The limiting Schwinger functions satisfy the OS axioms strongly enough to reconstruct H_YM, Omega, and H from the same continuum theory.
watched_milestones.success_signal: A reconstruction packet names the Hilbert space, vacuum, Hamiltonian/semigroup, observable domain, and positivity argument.
watched_milestones.why_big_deal: This would turn Euclidean data into the Hamiltonian arena where a mass gap has a precise spectral meaning.

certification_evidence: Observable is defined in the same limiting continuum object.
Connected or higher-order correlation does not vanish in the limit.
The witness distinguishes the result from a free Gaussian fixed point.
disqualifiers: The witness is only heuristic or simulation-level evidence.
The observable is not gauge invariant.
The nontriviality claim comes from a different approximation scheme than the constructed limit.
watched_milestones.label: Nontrivial interacting continuum theory witnessed
watched_milestones.next_action: Select one candidate gauge-invariant observable family and state the exact non-Gaussianity/nontriviality lemma it would need to satisfy.
watched_milestones.potentially_achieved_when: A gauge-invariant observable has limiting correlations or cumulants incompatible with the free/Gaussian theory.
watched_milestones.success_signal: A nonzero connected correlation, Wilson-loop area/perimeter behavior, or higher cumulant survives cutoff removal.
watched_milestones.why_big_deal: This would prevent an apparent construction from collapsing into a Gaussian, empty, or purely classical limit.

certification_evidence: The decay estimate is proved before and after taking the continuum limit.
The mass parameter m has a positive lower bound independent of cutoff scale.
The observable family is tied to the reconstructed physical Hilbert space.
disqualifiers: Decay is available only at strong coupling or fixed lattice spacing.
Constants degenerate to zero under cutoff removal.
The observable family is not spectrally determining.
watched_milestones.label: Cutoff-uniform Euclidean mass-gap witness obtained
watched_milestones.next_action: Turn the correlator route into a decay-to-gap lemma with explicit uniform constants and observable-density assumptions.
watched_milestones.potentially_achieved_when: Gauge-invariant Euclidean correlations decay exponentially with constants stable under continuum-limit passage.
watched_milestones.success_signal: A family of observables O has |<O(t)O(0)>_c| <= C_O exp(-m t) with m > 0 independent of the removed cutoff.
watched_milestones.why_big_deal: This would provide the first concrete spectral-gap witness rather than only a desired Hamiltonian inequality.

certification_evidence: H, Omega, and P_perp come from OS/Wightman reconstruction of the constructed Yang-Mills theory.
A decay-to-gap or direct spectral argument excludes all non-vacuum states below Delta.
Gauge-invariant observables determine the relevant excitation sector.
disqualifiers: The gap is only a finite-lattice transfer-matrix gap.
The spectral statement is asserted before Hilbert-space reconstruction.
The proof omits vacuum uniqueness or the projection onto non-vacuum excitations.
watched_milestones.label: Positive Hamiltonian spectral gap proved
watched_milestones.next_action: Use the Hamiltonian derivation as a checkpoint: list every premise needed before E_H((0, Delta)) P_perp = 0 can be claimed.
watched_milestones.potentially_achieved_when: The reconstructed Hamiltonian has no non-vacuum spectrum in (0, Delta) for some Delta > 0.
watched_milestones.success_signal: A theorem proves Spec(H restricted to P_perp H_YM) subset [Delta, infinity) for the same continuum theory.
watched_milestones.why_big_deal: This is the mass-gap half of the Clay target in the reconstructed physical Hilbert space.

certification_evidence: All upstream milestones cite the same limiting object and observable algebra.
No open proof obligation blocks a required Clay commitment.
Failure tests for cutoff leakage, triviality, and insufficient reconstruction all pass.
disqualifiers: Construction, nontriviality, and gap are proved in different theories.
Any essential target commitment is weakened without an accepted weakening rule.
The proof depends on an unvalidated heuristic or numerical premise.
watched_milestones.label: Same-theory Clay target integration achieved
watched_milestones.next_action: Keep this as the top-level success gate and only promote lower milestones when they preserve all essential commitments.
watched_milestones.potentially_achieved_when: Existence, nontriviality, OS/Wightman adequacy, continuum limit, and positive mass gap are proved for one and the same Yang-Mills theory.
watched_milestones.success_signal: A single dependency-closed proof packet connects all five essential commitments with no theory-switching or cutoff leakage.
watched_milestones.why_big_deal: This is the point where local successes stop being isolated and become a candidate solution architecture for the full problem.
